patch_description: The best prior variant (Kalman/RTS + guarded velocity clamp + sub-noise reversal damping) cut slope_changes from 29.2 to 20.4 and false_reversals from 23.0 to 14.2 versus the current two-pass baseline, at identical combined score (0.72) — but its correlation dipped slightly (0.92→0.89). Strategy: port the zero-phase velocity-aware displacement clamp and guarded reversal damping into the current (higher-accuracy) program, but keep the conservative correlation guards (>= 0.97) and a milder reversal-damp threshold so the accuracy/responsiveness metrics of the current version are preserved while the smoothness gains are captured. Additionally, harden the interface per the recommendation: n < window_size now returns a graceful fallback instead of raising, and NaN/inf inputs are sanitized — this eliminates the crash mode that zeroed out three of nine prior programs. All operations are zero-phase (bidirectional sweeps), so no lag is added.
